Indicator: Number of SAPS-owned firearms confirmed as stolen/lost
Outcome: Priority 6: Social Cohesion and Safer Communities
Cluster: Justice, Crime Prevention and Security cluster
AnnualTarget_Summary2: Reduce to 652 (10%)
ReasonforDeviation_Summary:
Target not achieved.

The Department has implemented several measures to reduce firearm losses, including providing members with safes and retention cords. Despite these efforts, the rise in robberies in townships and other areas, as well as incidents of housebreaking, vehicle theft, and personal theft, contribute to ongoing losses. Given the nature of police work, the risk of firearm loss is ever-present. It is the responsibility of each member to safeguard their issued firearm, following the preventive measures established by the department. Unfortunately, instances of firearm loss due to member negligence do occur, but every loss is thoroughly investigated regardless of the circumstances. Preventing firearm losses remains a top priority for the Department.
CorrectiveAction_Summary: Every loss is thoroughly investigated regardless of the circumstances.
ReasonforDeviation_Q1: The escalation of robbery in a township or other place, as well as housebreaking (property locked), negligence of members, theft from a dwelling, and loss from person.
CorrectiveAction_Q1: The bar coding and marking of all SAPS-owned firearms with the SAPS emblem, IBIS testing to create firearm profiles, biannual inspections, the issuing of safes to members for the safekeeping of firearms, the issuing of retention cords, daily parade inspections, control over and the safekeeping of firearms not under the direct and physical control of a member and inspections by designated supply chain personnel are all measures taken to prevent the loss of SAPS-owned firearms.
ReasonforDeviation_Q2: The escalation of robbery in a township or other place, as well as housebreaking (property locked), negligence of members, theft from a dwelling and loss from person.
CorrectiveAction_Q2: Implementation of relevant legislative requirements when incidents of lost firearms materialise. Official communication to provincial and divisional offices on the loss of firearms and follow-up monitoring letters. Biannual inspections and certification of all official firearms.
ReasonforDeviation_Q3: The escalation of robbery in a township or other place, as well as housebreaking (property locked), negligence of members, theft from a dwelling and loss from person.
CorrectiveAction_Q3: Measures taken to prevent the loss of SAPS-owned firearms, include the bar coding and the marking of all SAPS-owned firearms with the SAPS emblem, IBIS testing to create firearm profiles, biannual inspections, the issuing of safes to members for the safekeeping of firearms, the issuing of retention cords, daily parade inspections, control over and the safekeeping of firearms not under the direct and physical control of a member and inspections by Designated Supply Chain Management Armorers.
ReasonforDeviation_Q4: The escalation of robbery in a township or other place, as well as housebreaking (property locked), theft from a motor vehicle and loss from person.
CorrectiveAction_Q4: Measures taken to prevent the loss of SAPS-owned firearms, include the bar coding and the marking of all SAPS-owned firearms with the SAPS emblem, IBIS testing to create firearm profiles, biannual inspections, the issuing of safes to members for the safekeeping of firearms, the issuing of retention cords, daily parade inspections, control over and the safekeeping of firearms not under the direct and physical control of a member and inspections by Designated Supply Chain Management Armorers.

Indicator: Number of arrests for economic infrastructure-related crimes, for cases investigated by EITTs
Outcome: Priority 6: Social Cohesion and Safer Communities
Cluster: Justice, Crime Prevention and Security cluster
ReasonforDeviation_Summary:
Target not achieved.

In response to emerging threats concerning economic and essential infrastructure, including illegal mining, EITTs were established as an interim measure. These teams serve as a temporary solution while a work-study investigation on the permanent establishment of such capabilities is underway. However, the interim nature of this intervention has led to challenges in establishing optimal business processes and reporting channels, resulting in a heavy reliance on manual feedback processes. Despite these challenges, immediate monitoring and reporting were necessary, although this deviated from the ideal 
protocol of ensuring that performance information undergoes proper validation and testing before inclusion in the APP. The SAPS was thus compelled to set targets based on available baseline information at the time. Presently, efforts are underway to enhance the functioning of EITTs and improve reporting mechanisms to effectively report on successes achieved in addressing these critical threats.
CorrectiveAction_Summary: Efforts are underway to enhance the functioning of EITTs and improve reporting mechanisms.
ReasonforDeviation_Q3: Due to the fact that this is a new performance indicator, an Excel reporting template was developed and made available to the EITT Teams. However, some individuals are not acquainted with the reporting template's completion process due to their limited understanding of the concepts of APPs, TIDs, datasets and data schedules, as well as their lack of familiarity with the template itself.
CorrectiveAction_Q3: Building capacity through workshops/engagement session. The restatement of performance will occur subsequent to the conclusion of the capacity building session and receipt of all-inclusive reporting templates from the EITTs.
ReasonforDeviation_Q4: The annual target established for the 2023/24 financial year was deemed inaccurate, as it was based on unverifiable data inclusive of cases reported at the districts in which the EITTs were situated, rather than actual cases that the EITTs themselves investigated.
CorrectiveAction_Q4: During a work session attended by all relevant role players and EITT coordinators, TIDs and reporting requirements were discussed and challenges were brought to the attention of the Head: Strategic Management.

PrelimaryAudited_Summary2: 30 650 vehicles were recovered, including 29 812 identified vehicles, 666 unidentified vehicles and 172 cross-border vehicles.
ReasonforDeviation_Summary:
Target not achieved.

The decline in stolen vehicles being recovered by the police can be attributed to several key factors. Criminals are increasingly employing sophisticated theft methods, such as electronic hacking or rapid disassembly in ‘chop shops’, making vehicles harder to track and retrieve. International trafficking networks further complicate recovery efforts, with vehicles often crossing borders swiftly or being sold abroad. Limited police resources and personnel dedicated to vehicle theft investigations also hamper recovery rates. Additionally, technology deficiencies and organised crime involvement pose significant challenges to law enforcement.
CorrectiveAction_Summary: In order to accurately capture performance information in respect of the recovery of stolen and robbed vehicles, measures were taken to amend SAPS systems and Standard Operating Procedures. Audit findings in this regard demonstrated that non-compliance to adhere to the revised procedures results in the omission of some recoveries in performance information, which leads to underreporting. A letter will be drafted to those provinces that failed to meet the target. The tracking and tracing of stolen/robbed vehicles and tampered vehicles, and the disposal of vehicles in Vehicle Safeguarding Units is the responsibility of the detective environment. SAPS members at the district and police station levels, Vehicle Safeguarding Units and Vehicle Crime Investigation Units will receive in-service training and guidance from the visible policing and detective environment regarding the capturing of stolen/robbed recovered vehicles on the SAPS Circulation System during scheduled visits and the evaluation of units in the 2024/25 financial year.

This will have the effect of understating performance and contribute to audit findings.
CorrectiveAction_Q1: A letter will be sent to all of the provinces that did not meet their targets. The capturing of vehicles as "placed in police custody" will be re-emphasised. Improvements to the Circulation System: vehicles will be workshopped at all Vehicle Safeguarding Services (VSS) and provincial coordinators will be required to continuously assess the implementation of the instruction at VSS and at stations. ReasonforDeviation_Summary:

The reported incidence of contact crime may not be a direct or reliable indicator of police performance. While it is important to track crime rates, it is essential to consider various factors that can affect these statistics. Crime rates are influenced by a range of complex factors and in particular violent or contact crime, including socio-economic conditions, inequality, education levels, drug abuse, community dynamics and more. 

Addressing these underlying causes of crime requires long-term economic, social and developmental interventions that extend beyond the scope of immediate police responses. Police responses primarily focus on dealing with the symptoms of the problem by enforcing the law, apprehending offenders and maintaining public order. While these efforts are necessary, they are not sufficient to address the root causes of crime, comprehensively.
CorrectiveAction_Summary: The SAPS initiated Operation Shanela, in May 2023, based on an Enhanced Crime Prevention and Combating Action Plan (ICPCAP). The Plan and Operation Shanela provides for coordinated weekly mandatory (simultaneous and high density) integrated and multidisciplinary operations in priority police station areas. Operation Shanela and the ICPCAP also provide for increased community mobilisation against crime in collaboration with Community Police Forums, focusing on the top 30 national and top 10 provincial police stations contributing to the highest reported incidence of contact crime and Gender-Based Violence (GBV). In addition, Operation Shanela targets wanted suspects sought for murder, GBV and other serious crimes.

Applications for security clearance that had reached an advanced stage were placed on hold pending service provider approval.
CorrectiveAction_Q1: The evaluations capacity will be enhanced through the assistance of provincial vetting personnel, in order to increase the performance output, in relation to security clearance applications.
ReasonforDeviation_Q2: According to the previous Standard Operating Procedures for Vetting Evaluation processes, working with outdated information in outdated files was not in accordance with target-based performance, resulting in a backlog. A total of 98 security clearances were completed in the second quarter only.
CorrectiveAction_Q2: Review of the SOPs in order to take the appropriate measures to address underperformance. The appointment of nine vetting officers to the Section Vetting through Post Promotions Phase 1: 2023-2024.
ReasonforDeviation_Q3: The delay in the finalisation of security clearances is as a result of the e-vetting system which is not user friendly for both applicants and end-users, which affects the turn around time to meet the set target. Although the planned target of 75% for quarter three was not achieved, there is a marginal improvement on the finalisation of security clearances. A total of 150 applications were finalised in the 3rd quarter only, compared to 95 that were finalised in the first quarter and 98 in second quarter, respectively.
CorrectiveAction_Q3: The appointment of the Section Head: Vetting to enhance command and control, developing the vetting policy, review the Standard Operating Procedure and the e-vetting system. The appointment of nine vetting officers through post promotions and the deployment of provincial vetting personnel to Head Office has contributed to the marginal increase on the finalisation of security clearances. The deployment of provincial vetting personnel to the Head Office project will continue until 31 March 2024, in order to increase the performance output, in relation to security clearance applications.
ReasonforDeviation_Q4: The successful completion of the security clearances was facilitated by the Vetting Intervention Project, the appointment of nine vetting officers and the appointment of the Section Head: Vetting.

Furthermore, the turnaround time for the submission of evaluation reports by technical experts and the processing of committee recommendations immediately after the adoption of minutes will be stringently monitored.
ReasonforDeviation_Q1: The period during which applications were received for this APP target was 23 Nov 2022 to 22 Feb 2023. CorrectiveAction_Q1: Continued engagements to ensure speedy appointment of new committee member and prioritising of final documentation, coding fixes to deal with online system issue.
ReasonforDeviation_Q2: The period during which applications were received for this APP target was 24 Feb 2023 to 26 May 2023.  Challenges having an impact include reduced number of meetings due to quorum issues (for last 2 quarters) and online system not being available during last quarter due to generator issues.
CorrectiveAction_Q2: Continued engagement with IT to move online system to Cloud. Continued monitoring of all other aspects having intermittent impact on turnaround time, including ensuring quorums for meetings, prioritising of final documentation, coding fixes to deal with online system issues and signoff of batches.
ReasonforDeviation_Q3: The period during which applications were received for this APP target was 24 May 2023 to 22 Aug. 2023. Challenges include some minor online system issues and the carry-over from previous quarter, as well as staff movement, as well as delays in the sign-off of letters.
CorrectiveAction_Q3: The online system was moved to the Cloud during this quarter, which should negate the impact of loadshedding. A new assistant is being trained on the system and all processes are now up to date. It is important to ensure that the online system is updated as soon as possible so that applications received quarter 4 can be processed through the online system.
ReasonforDeviation_Q4: The period during which applications were received for this APP target was October 2023 to 31 December 2023.  Challenges include some minor online system issues and carry over challenges from the previous quarter,  staff movement and very short December impacting signoff of letters.
CorrectiveAction_Q4: Improved user support on reported online system technical issues as well as stringent monitoring  measures on (1) turnaround time  for submission of evaluation reports by technical experts; and (2) processing committee recommendations immediately after adoption of minutes
